title: The Register Calls It Something Else
request: Our slips say card; the old register says member_no. Same numbers, stubborn clerks. Match them anyway and deliver the title with the borrower's name, sorted by title.
objective: Join tables whose key columns carry different labels.
hints: Nothing matches while you insist both tables spell the key the same way.
join takes a third argument naming the key column in the other table.
Join on card with member_no as the other label, then select the title and name columns and sort by title.
inputCode:
import random
from datascience import Table, make_array
names = ['Gideon Plume', 'Halla Brine', 'Isolde Marrow', 'Jarek Quill', 'Kesia Ardent']
cards = [107, 108, 109, 110, 111]
titles = ['Nine Ways to Fold a Map', 'Winter Comes to the Aviary', 'The Lamp Under the Stair', 'Eleven Rooms of Rain', 'Lanterns of the Slow Tide', 'A Short History of Waiting']
size = random.randint(3, 5)
chosen = sorted(random.sample(range(5), size))
register = Table().with_columns('member_no', make_array(*[cards[index] for index in chosen]), 'name', make_array(*[names[index] for index in chosen]))
n = random.randint(3, 6)
shelf_titles = random.sample(titles, n)
slips = Table().with_columns('title', make_array(*shelf_titles), 'card', make_array(*[cards[random.choice(chosen)] for _ in range(n)]))

rows: Nine Ways to Fold a Map
